ArticleRank

Source: R/centrality-batch68.R
centrality_articlerank.Rd

ArticleRank (Li and Willett 2009) is a PageRank-style score for citation networks in which a citing node passes on its score in a share set by its number of references: $$AR(A) = 1 - d + d\,\overline{NR} \sum_{P \to A} \frac{AR(P)}{\overline{NR} + NR(P)},$$ with \(P \to A\) when \(P\) cites \(A\), \(NR(P)\) the number of references of \(P\), \(\overline{NR}\) its mean over the nodes and \(d\) the damping factor.

Usage

centrality_articlerank(x, ...)

Arguments

x

Network input accepted by centrality.

...

Further arguments to centrality. The measure uses ar_references (the number of references of each node, default the out-degree) and damping (default 0.85).

Value

A named numeric vector with one score per node, in input node order.

Details

The measure uses the direction of the arcs and ignores weights; an undirected tie is an arc each way, and loops are ignored. This is equation (2) of the source, with the mean number of references as a multiplier; the Centrality Zoo prints the form without it, which the source's printed numbers rule out. The source counts all the references of a paper, also those outside the network, so ar_references takes one count per node (in node order, or named by node); NULL, the default, takes the out-degree (owner decision 2026-11-26). damping is \(d\), 0.85 by default as in the source. The scores are not normalised; a node nobody cites scores \(1 - d\). The source iterates the equation from \(1 - d\) to a precision of \(10^{-10}\); that iteration converges, to the solution of the linear system computed here, exactly when the spectral radius of its linear map is below 1. A citation network without cycles has radius 0. A cyclic network can have radius 1 or more, an undirected one as soon as its degrees are large (an undirected network where every node has degree \(k\) and the references are the degrees has radius \(dk/2\)); the score then has no value, and the measure warns (class cograph_undefined_measure) and returns NA rather than switching to another form. The implementation reproduces the 13 terms \(AR(P)/(\overline{NR} + NR(P))\) of the source's Table 5 whose citing paper is not cited itself, and, on a citation network built so that the 46 citing papers of Table 5 have their printed scores, the printed difference between the scores of papers P004 and P005 (0.49716); with the same citing scores, the form without the multiplier gives a difference 35.6 times smaller. On the four undirected test networks of the other measures' screens the score has no value; oriented from lower to higher node number, the four have Kendall correlations of at most 0.24 in absolute value between this score and any other measure. An ar_references that is not one finite nonnegative number per node, or whose names do not match the nodes, raises a cograph_bad_parameter error, as do references that are all zero on a network with arcs. normalized = TRUE divides the scores by their maximum.

References

Li, J. and Willett, P. (2009). ArticleRank: a PageRank-based alternative to numbers of citations for analysing citation networks. Aslib Proceedings, 61(6), 605-618. doi:10.1108/00012530911005544 .

See also

centrality_pagerank, centrality.

Examples

# Four papers: B, C and D cite A, and D cites B.
citations <- matrix(c(0, 0, 0, 0,  1, 0, 0, 0,  1, 0, 0, 0,  1, 1, 0, 0), 4, byrow = TRUE,
                    dimnames = list(LETTERS[1:4], LETTERS[1:4]))
centrality_articlerank(citations)
#>         A         B         C         D 
#> 0.3380625 0.1925000 0.1500000 0.1500000 
centrality_articlerank(citations, ar_references = c(A = 12, B = 30, C = 8, D = 45))
#>         A         B         C         D 
#> 0.3622993 0.1940455 0.1500000 0.1500000 
centrality_articlerank(regulation_net, damping = 0.5)
#>    Explore       Plan    Monitor      Adapt    Reflect    Discuss Synthesize 
#>   2.335585   1.209805   2.729098   2.056152   2.045531   1.240876   1.014038 
#>   Evaluate     Create      Share 
#>   1.124507   1.855787   1.825183
